In mouse emulator mode I was previously using orthogonal projection and trying to compensate with an exponent. This math was wrong, I am now using the correct math for perspective projection. This also gets rid of the horizontal and vertical exponent sliders.

notes.title: 0.95 - Mouse Emulator mode now playable
notes.notes:
I believe I've fixed all the major issues with using the Mouse Emulator mode in games. In hindsight I listed the mode on my website a few weeks too early and this is the first version that is truly playable.

It uses Track IR for both head rotation and movement. Track IR isn't ideal because it wasn't designed for the distances I am using it at. I may write my own system, however it would incur a significant performance cost while Track IR takes very little performance relatively speaking.

Voice Attack is used for all commands other than looking and moving. Voice attack also isn't ideal, as it can fail commands. But it's the best that is available. I haven't found a way to put buttons on my gun that also do not disrupt the shooting experience. Will keep thinking about solutions.

[list]
[*] Integrated TrackIR directly into Interactive Gun Range, which  does a better job than Free Pie of providing smooth mouse input
[*] It was too difficult to play first person shooters using a dancepad, so added the ability to control WADS and a virtual gamepad by physically stepping forward, left, back, right respectively. This also makes the setup process easier, removing the need to buy a dance pad.
[/list]
Add saveable and loadable presets to mouse emulator mode. Add mouse speed exponent property

[list]
[*] Display is now brighter on average on PC.
[*] Improve friendliness of brightness calibration.
[*] Mouse emulator add game presets.
[/list]

[list]
[*] Make starting calibration even more friendly
[*] Have the user shoot a required 4 shots during sight offset calibration, and interpolate a quadilateral to use this data for greater accuracy.
[/list]

[list]
[*] Many small fixes, mostly for mobile but some improve the PC version
[*] Previously factory reset was not actually deleting everything. Now it does.
[*] You are now required to use compensated sights, this is to fix bad alignment from extreme camera angles
[*] Calibration flow for paper scale and distance from display now looks a little nicer
[/list]

[list]
[*] Make calibration a little easier to understand for people who don't like to read.
[*] During camera selection, you can no longer pick unsuitable cameras. These are tested and hidden.
[/list]

[list]
[*] It is no longer necessary to open Logi Tune or even buy a Logitech camera, exposure calibration is done automatically.
[*] Added more settings to mouse emulator mode
[/list]

[list]
[*]You can now control how much time has to pass between shots in the options screen, allowing fast shooters to reach a higher par time.
[*]Shots are now much more accurate towards the edges of the screen
[*]Mouse emulator mode is now compatible with more games, and more games are presented to the user.
[*]Android support has been completed and should be public within a day or so.
[/list]

This adds the Mouse Emulator game mode for Windows. This game mode allows you to play other games, using the gun's laser as a mouse. The mode effectively adds compatibility with thousands of other games, using your real gun.

[list]
[*] Added display mode options
[*] Added option to turn off the mouse cursor, for use with the Sinden light gun
[/list]

This version adds mouse support. The purpose is not to actually play with the mouse, but to play with the Sinden Light gun which emulates the mouse. The Sinden Light Gun has many advantages over a laser, such as not needing a separate webcam, not needing calibration, running during the day at full brightness, and it's cheap relative to the other accessories. The disadvantage is you are not using your real gun, which limits training value, and it only works on the Windows version of IGR.

See [url=https://interactivegunrange.com/sindenwithigr/]https://interactivegunrange.com/sindenwithigr/[/url] for details on how to set this up.
Slightly easier calibration for exposure.

This build adds preliminary iOS support. While that may not be of interest on Steam, I had to make many improvements to calibration generally to get it to work. As a result, it is now possible under good conditions to run your display at maximum brightness, without any false negatives or positives.

[list]
[*] Improved calibration generally
[*] New exposure setup screen to help users setup calibration more easily
[/list]

[list]
[*] Improved exposure handling
[*] Fix bug where shots were not presented to user during distance training between targets
[/list]

[list]
[*] Improved detection of lasers with inconsistent brightness
[*] Update 'Get Help' from main menu to be more helpful
[*] Now accurately report camera framerate during camera selection screen
[*] Quit with an error if the camera has too low of a framerate for the game to be playable
[/list]
Further fixes and clarifies how to setup brightness and exposure during calibration
Attempting to fix how the game handles camera exposure. Ideally, users can run at normal brightness when the correct values are set.

[list]

[/list]

[list]

[/list]

[list][*][p]New Distance Training Game mode. Insprired by my time at a class were we were shooting at 100 yard steel targets with a pistol.[/p][/*][*][p]Calibration now better accounts for auto-exposure and display brightness. In addtion, there was a bug I added a while ago that disabled the screen brightness adjustment. That is now fixed.[/p][/*][/list]

[*] Add optional sight offset compensation screen, run during calibration. This adjusts the processed laser hit point to match the sights on your gun.

notes.notes:
[list]
[*] I reworked Shoot / No Shoot. The training principle is the same, which is target identification, but it works in a more sensible way now and attempts to teach the player.

Mostly UI fixes to pass the Mac store review
Slightly improved false positives when using inconsistently bright lasers.

Improved compatibility with Dry Fire Mag. However, Dry Fire Mag only works if setting the camera to 800x600 @ 60 FPS. 800x600 @ 60 FPS is only supported on desktop (mobile devices are locked to 30 FPS). The higher framerate is because the laser strike of Dry Fire Mag is too short, and can get missed between camera updates.
The shooting part of calibration now takes fewer shots and is easier to perform
Screen is now brighter during gameplay, especially when using a consistently bright pistol, such as a SIRT pistol
False negatives should now be eliminated, at a slightly smaller chance of false positives.
